name: LangChain
title: Support and onboarding that help teams ship useful agents
subtitle: Customer success · LangGraph workflows · LangSmith evaluation
focus: Ground technical help in evidence, turn repeated onboarding friction into a tested workflow and connect adoption to customer outcomes.
priorities: Build agents and automation for support, onboarding and customer success.
Use LangGraph and LangSmith for reliable, observable workflows.

layers: Customer question, environment and exact product / documentation context.
Relevant approved documentation and trace evidence with version information.
Grounding, privacy, task success and escalation checks before a response.
Human-reviewed help, onboarding milestones and product feedback with observability.
rules: A source link alone does not prove the answer is supported.
Escalate missing context, failed evaluations and account-sensitive actions.
Do not treat framework downloads as a verified company expansion signal.

personas.name: Developer / builder
personas.pain: A specific technical blocker between an agent idea and a useful deployment
personas.promise: A relevant source, the missing context and a clear next debugging step.
personas.subject: The next step for {{workflow}}
personas.email: Hi {{first_name}}, I’m following up on the {{question_type}} question. Could you share the minimal environment and the step that fails? I’d like to connect the relevant documentation to a reproducible next step, then escalate anything the evidence does not support.
personas.question: What is the smallest reproducible case, and which version or environment is involved?

personas.name: Customer success / platform owner
personas.pain: Adoption across teams without a clear success milestone
personas.promise: A shared onboarding plan with evaluated help and an explicit human owner.
personas.subject: A useful milestone for {{team}}
personas.email: Hi {{first_name}}, I’d like to make the next adoption milestone concrete: a representative trace, a reviewed evaluation set, or a deployed workflow that the team can judge. Which one would move your current use case forward?
personas.question: What observable milestone would make the next success review useful?

pitch: I am an AI product builder with an enterprise sales background. I have shipped a revenue-generating iOS app, built a source-backed extraction pipeline and compared models on grounding, structured output and total workflow cost. At LangChain, I would start with a narrow support or onboarding problem, a reviewed evaluation set and an observable workflow that helps a customer complete a useful task.
mappings: Hey Sammy: model comparison, source grounding, validation and recovery.
Evaluate a narrow support task before expanding automation.
Shipped app onboarding and dependable product workflows.
Define the next observable customer milestone.
Enterprise sales, partnerships and direct work with technical stakeholders.
Understand the actual customer task and return useful context to engineering.
northStar: Customers completing useful tasks with evidence-grounded help
weekOne: One support question category with a grounded answer path, evaluations and a human escalation route.
days60: Extend the evaluated workflow to a second onboarding milestone and improve observability and integration recovery.
days90: Make customer-success and product feedback repeatable, then prioritize expansion of the support system from task success and customer usefulness.

firstBuilds.title: Grounded support workflow
firstBuilds.goal: Help with one repeatable question and escalate the rest.
firstBuilds.scope: One onboarding question category and a reviewed evaluation set.
firstBuilds.measure: Supported answers, task completion, correct escalation and time to useful help.

firstBuilds.title: Milestone-led onboarding
firstBuilds.goal: Make the next useful step explicit for the customer team.
firstBuilds.scope: A small developer cohort moving from trace to evaluation or deployment.
firstBuilds.measure: Milestone completion, repeated blockers and customer usefulness.

firstBuilds.title: Product feedback loop
firstBuilds.goal: Convert recurring support friction into useful engineering context.
firstBuilds.scope: One weekly customer-success / product review with clear ownership.
firstBuilds.measure: Actionable reports, duplicates, resolved patterns and follow-through.

projectRelevance.sammy: Model comparisons, grounding checks, structured extraction and resumable jobs are directly relevant to reliable support-agent design.
projectRelevance.sidequest: Recoverable product workflows, analytics and careful content delivery connect engineering decisions to customer experience.
projectRelevance.dancers: Private inquiry flows, durable notifications and delivery recovery illustrate why reliable state and human ownership matter.
